The Rebbe started the letter by saying, I was happy to get your letter that you wrote in English. Continue writing, especially about good news.

Next, the Rebbe wrote about how happy he was to hear that the person was adding in Torah and mitzvos, and the Rebbe encouraged him to do even more. The Rebbe also wrote that giving tzedakah will take away worries about parnassah, and that he was looking forward to hearing good news about the new baby.

Tatty held the letter with trembling hands. Writing in English? Adding in Torah and mitzvos? Parnassah worries going away? A bracha for the new baby? It felt like the Rebbe was speaking directly to him, answering everything he had written about in his letter.

This was Tatty’s first time writing a really long, personal letter to the Rebbe, and the Rebbe had found a way to answer him.

Three months later, on the night that Tatty finished saying Kaddish for Zeidy, Mommy gave birth to Mottel, who was the first grandchild to be named after Zeidy.

Each one of us feels so proud to have had such a special Zeidy, and we do all that we can to follow in his footsteps, preparing the world for Moshiach.

As kids, we might not be able to write to the Rebbe in the same way that grown-ups do. But that’s ok! We can connect with the Rebbe in whatever way we can, in whatever language we know. The Rebbe wants to hear from each of his chassidim—and he will find a way to answer.

Tatty sat deep in thought, writing a long letter to the Rebbe. A few days later, he knew without a doubt that the Rebbe had heard him.

When Zeidy Berger suddenly passed away at the age of 66, Tatty’s life changed forever.

You see, our Zeidy was a very special chossid of the Rebbe. He was the first shliach to Ottawa, Canada, and he spent his life spreading Torah and Chassidus to hundreds of Yidden.

Brokenhearted that Zeidy had passed away, Tatty decided to do all he could to continue in his ways.

My father was so devoted to the Rebbe, he thought. He spent his entire life helping Yidden learn

Torah and do mitzvos to bring Moshiach, and I want to do the same.

From then on, Tatty started living each day with a mission to bring the Geulah, just like Zeidy. He learned more Torah, did more mitzvos, and helped other Yidden connect with their Yiddishkeit.

That Pesach, Tatty and Mommy flew to New York and visited the Ohel. At the time, they were expecting their second child.

When Tatty sat down to write a letter to the Rebbe, he felt a deep connection that he had never felt before. Instead of writing a short letter in Hebrew like he always did, he found himself writing a long, emotional letter to the Rebbe in English, describing the ups and downs of the past few months and telling the Rebbe about everything he had done to bring Moshiach closer. He also wrote about the worries he had about his parnassah.

Mottel, 9 Henna Berger, 8 Cheder Menachem & Bais Chaya Mushka, LA
